name: Boldo
summary: Boldo (Peumus boldus) carries a Grade C rating — limited evidence. Strongest recorded design is a narrative review, drawn from 1 recorded study, none of which measured an outcome in people. Recorded activity centres on digestive support and hepatobiliary support, which describes mechanism rather than demonstrated benefit. Noted cautions include pregnancy or breastfeeding without clinician guidance.
description: Boldo botanical profile with evidence, safety, and practical fit.
contraindications: liver disease or bile duct disease or gallstones due to contraindicated biliary obstruction risk and hepatotoxic ascaridole content
anticoagulant medication such as warfarin due to a coumarin-type interaction that may enhance anticoagulant effect and increase bleeding risk
pregnancy or breastfeeding without clinician guidance
unprocessed high-ascaridole boldo products due to rare hepatotoxicity case reports including jaundice or hepatic injury and should be avoided in favor of ascaridole-free commercial extracts
